comparison.objective: Candidate sets and locks an angular-gripper stop; PR-741 inserts a stripped cable into a lug, actuates a crimping press, removes the terminated cable, and returns it to its rest.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires two concentric tools and countertorque during locking; PR-741 requires depth-and-axis-controlled cable insertion held while another hand closes a lever press.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires retained 90° opening over three cycles with low drift and retained nuts; PR-741 requires prescribed insertion depth and alignment at crimp, release, removal, rest placement, and in later versions a real pull test.
comparison.reason: Holding an inserted cable while operating a crimper does not test locking a continuous adjustment against coupled jam-nut torque or retained articulated motion; all spec versions state observable criteria.
